ai.description: *Cyrtodactylus adleri* reaches 75 mm SVL. It is brownish with dark, irregular dorsal blotches and a distinct pale nuchal collar. Key features include slender, curved toes and a granular dorsal texture.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Cyrtodactylus adleri* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, continuous dark nuchal loop that remains unbroken behind the head, unlike many similar congeners.
ai.habitat: *Cyrtodactylus adleri* inhabits the moist deciduous forests of the Andaman Islands, typically found at low elevations on tree trunks or among rocky outcrops.
ai.behavior: Cyrtodactylus adleri is a nocturnal gecko that spends its nights actively foraging for small invertebrates among the rocky crevices of its karst habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Cyrtodactylus adleri* is oviparous, laying a clutch of two eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, typically between June and August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Cyrtodactylus adleri* is endemic to the high-altitude regions of Arunachal Pradesh in Northeast India, typically occurring at elevations between 1,500 and 2,000 meters.
